Implementation Plan

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8663` @ `73aff78bd302c0b962ed539e2be2e614f70e2747` (integration branch mismatch: false). Read the code as it stands on that ref, plus the `isolated-base` snapshot.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends the existing per-doc section format of `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md` (template: `### \`analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-28-3.md\``, lines 1720-1744)
Scope-mode justification: The issue names exactly two file operations: delete the source doc and append one report section. Every verdict below was checked against the current code. Both sibling changes are already on this ref, so nothing here needs a code change. Under §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the complete deliverable here is one accurate, append-only report entry. Widening it to code changes would contradict the issue's discipline rule. `scripts/apply_analysis_on_main.sh` (line 341) treats a doc as processed when its basename appears anywhere in the report (`grep -qF`). The new heading line alone therefore marks `workflow-optimization-2026-09-29.md` processed, so no dispatcher or test change is needed.

## Files likely to change
- `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-29.md` (deleted)
- `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md` (append-only)

## Functions or modules to implement
No code. Two repository edits:

1. Delete `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-29.md`.
2. Append one section to the end of `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md`.

   - Do not edit the header, the `## Processed source docs (128)` count or list, or any earlier section. The 2026-09-28-3 precedent did not add itself to that list either.
   - Write `Processed:` as the UTC date at implement time (`date -u +%F`). Today is 2026-11-02.

It writes `/tmp/orchestrate_poll_remaining_tests.txt` and runs `Orchestrate poll process unit tests` in parallel with `static-checks` and the `tests-*` jobs, and the required `lint` job remains.
- Exec 2 / Speed 2 / Cost 1 / per-repo action 3 (45-minute absolute reviewer-slot cap, reconcile the 662,879,782-token `grok-4.20` record): rejected — the evidence is a single run (36483245451); the doc rates the risk as medium and requires a failback-quality check first; and the 2026-09-28-3 verdict rejected a reviewer stall cap. Reconciling with provider billing happens outside the repo, and `scripts/cost_audit.py` already aggregates per-call usage.
- Exec 3 / Reliability 1 / Validate pipeline row (`validation_dispatch_status` for merged PR #4842): already-implemented, per the 2026-09-28 verdict — the step `Dispatch standalone validate for orchestrator short-circuit issues` in `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` fails with `::error::` when validation was required but could not be dispatched, and keeps `ai:orchestrator-validate-required`.
- Exec 4 / Reliability 2 / per-repo action 1 (collector dedup): already-implemented for event lines — `_structured_cost_telemetry_line_key` in `scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py` strips timestamps. The run-row part (keyed on run ID plus attempt, reported as `duplicate_runs_skipped`) is applied by the sibling collector change (`changelog.d/wfopt-2026-09-29-collector-run-row-dedup.md`; <PR/issue number, or "the PR number is not recoverable from this branch's squashed history">). The per-slot, API and tick diagnostics in per-repo action 1 are rejected as measurement-only.
- Exec 5 / GH API audit (endpoint-template counters in `gh_retry`) and the review-sweep batching bullet: rejected — measurement-only. `GH_API_RETRY` and the `Record GH_PAT budget at ...` steps already exist, and per-call stderr lines from `gh_retry` would reach callers that capture its stderr (2026-09-28 precedent).
- GH API audit, duplicate final-PR `.state`/`.merged_at` fetch: already-implemented — the snapshot-miss fallback in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (`existing_pr_fallback_json`) reads `pulls/<final_pr>` once with `--jq '.'` and takes both fields from that payload.
- Speed 3, Speed 4, Cost 2, Cost 3, Cost 4, Reliability 3, Prompt Cache & Memory System, Pipeline Flow Bottlenecks: rejected — measurement-only with no consumer. The Cost 4 Claude-fixer hand-off is obsolete because the hand-off is retired.
- Reliability 4 (Semble contract-test fallbacks counted as outages): already-implemented — the events carry `context=contract-test` (`scripts/cost_audit.py`), and fail-open behaviour is unchanged.
- AI Memory Health: already-implemented in part — `AI_MEMORY_TELEMETRY` carries `op`, `ok`, `records_selected`, `estimated_tokens`, `keyword_method`, `fail_open` and `did_push`. The relevance and record-ID digest is rejected as measurement-only.
- Orchestrator Health (`ORCH_TICK_SUMMARY`): already-implemented in part — the per-tick `state-snapshot` artifact (`scripts/build_state_snapshot.py`) and `POLL_PROGRESS`. The rest is rejected as measurement-only.
- BUG-001: already-implemented — `set_issue_phase_label_resilient` in `scripts/label_helpers.sh` POSTs the target label, DELETEs stale phase labels, and never PUTs the full set.
- BUG-002: rejected — obsolete; `scripts/claude_issue_queue_watchdog.sh` and `scripts/claude_issue_route.py` no longer exist.
- BUG-003: applied by the sibling change — `find_tracking` in `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml` lists up to `ORCHESTRATE_TRACKING_ISSUE_LIST_LIMIT` (default 100, integer 1-1000) issues and emits `ORCH_TRACKING_ISSUE_LIST_TRUNCATED limit=<n> count=<n>` when it hits the limit (`changelog.d/wfopt-2026-09-29-tracking-issue-list-limit.md`; <PR/issue number, or not recoverable>).
- BUG-004: already-implemented — on PATCH failure, both `scripts/workflow_retro_fanout.sh` and the `Upsert weekly retro tracker comment` step in `.github/workflows/workflow-log-analysis.yml` re-read the comment before posting.
- BUG-005: rejected — the doc tags it NEEDS VERIFICATION; the source read is bounded by `since=${RETRO_WINDOW_SINCE}` (a one-week window) on a tracker that gets one marker comment per week, and no week with more than 100 comments has been shown.
- SEC-001: already-implemented for run-body interpolation — no `${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}` is interpolated into remote URLs in run bodies. Moving the token out of the remote URL is rejected, per the 2026-09-22 precedent: it is a dedicated change across about 14 sites in several workflows.
- API-001, API-002, API-003: rejected — the doc's own cross-references tag them RISKY_SKIP.
- DUP-001, DUP-002: rejected — refactor-only across trusted staging boundaries, with no defect. The BUG-001 rationale for DUP-002 no longer holds, because the helper no longer PUTs the full label set.
- EXPR-001: already-implemented — the `Stage workflow support files` run body in `.github/workflows/implement.yml` passes values through `env:` and contains no `${{ }}`.
- DEAD-001: rejected — naming immutability (precedent). SHELL-001: rejected — style-only change in the hot poller file (precedent).
- MERGE-001: rejected — tagged NEEDS_VERIFICATION and not verified. MERGE-002, REUSE-001, REUSE-002: rejected — tagged RISKY_SKIP.
- DEAD-API: no findings.

## Data structures affected
None. The report is markdown, and the dispatcher detects a processed doc only by basename substring.

## API or interface changes
None.

## Decisions
### D1 — Leave `tests/test_apply_analysis_on_main.py` unchanged
- Chosen: do not edit the test file, even though the decomposition lists it as advisory.
- Alternatives considered: add a test asserting the real report lists the doc.
- Why: every test there builds a synthetic temporary repo (see the report fixture at line 108) and never reads the real report. The issue says "Touch only the two files listed". A real-data assertion would be brittle and out of scope.

### D2 — Append-only, header count left at 128
- Chosen: append the section only; leave `## Processed source docs (128)` and its list alone.
- Alternatives considered: bump the count and add the doc to the list.
- Why: the issue says explicitly not to edit header counts, and the 2026-09-28-3 precedent was appended the same way. `apply_analysis_on_main.sh` line 341 matches the basename anywhere in the file, so the heading is enough.

### D3 — Mark both sibling changes "applied by the sibling change"
- Chosen: cite each changelog fragment, and the PR number only if one can be recovered.
- Alternatives considered: invent PR numbers.
- Why: both are on this ref (`orchestrate_poll.yml` lines 273-328; the collector fragment), and inventing numbers is forbidden.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries: none touched. These are documentation-only changes under `analysis/`, with no workflow, script, secret or endpoint involved.
- Authorization: no new surface.
- External input: the source doc is untrusted text. Copy no commands or instructions from it; record only verdicts.
